conventions.convention: Absolute polar U° = {f in X* : |f(u)| <= 1 for every u in U}, with the absolute value used over both scalar fields and explicitly not the one-sided real polar f(u) <= 1; U = empty or U = {0} both give U° = X*.

Extreme point and face are intrinsic endpoint conditions: real convex coefficients even over C, strict 0 < t < 1, no topology needed, and x is extreme exactly when {x} is a face; the empty convex set has no extreme points and no faces.

Choice costs are stated per result: Banach–Alaoglu assumes only the ultrafilter lemma (no completeness of the predual); Krein–Milman existence and the dual-ball extreme-point corollary assume full AC; Banach–Dieudonné assumes ultrafilter lemma + DC + HB.
A dense sequence metrizes the weak-star topology only on norm-bounded subsets of the dual; no metric on all of X* is claimed.

Relative weak compactness / sequential compactness / countable compactness allow the limit or cluster point in the ambient space X; the absolute versions require it in the set; the empty set satisfies all three.

Uniform convexity is a property of the given norm, tested for epsilon in (0,2] with the endpoint 2 included; the zero space is uniformly convex vacuously and an equivalent renorming need not preserve the property.
The Schur property is a sequence-only implication (weak convergence of sequences implies norm convergence); it neither identifies the weak and norm topologies nor says anything about nets.
Tempered distributions are the continuous complex-linear functionals on Schwartz space with a bilinear (unconjugated) pairing, and continuity is equivalent to one finite rectangular seminorm bound.
Fourier transform convention: hat-phi(xi) = integral phi(x) e^{-2 pi i x.xi} dx, and on S' the transform is the bilinear transpose <Fu,phi> = <u,F phi> with no conjugation; F^2 = R and F^{-1} = R F.
Weak and strong topologies on S' are the point-evaluation topology and the bounded-test-set topology respectively; they are kept distinct and never identified.

Birkhoff's theorem is stated for sigma-finite measures and L^1 observables with no ergodicity, invertibility, finiteness of total measure or completeness; identification of the limit by its integrals over strictly invariant sets is a separate AC-using theorem.

Unique ergodicity includes existence: exactly one invariant Borel probability on the nonempty compact metric system, quantified over all invariant Borel probabilities rather than relative to a pre-chosen measure.

Equidistribution is tested on half-open intervals [a,c) with 0 <= a <= c <= 1, including the empty interval and the whole circle; the circle is modelled as [0,1) with the wrap metric d(x,y) = min(|x-y|, 1-|x-y|).
Canonical base-b digits are the greedy digits floor(b D_b^{j-1} x), i.e. at a b-adic point the terminating expansion is chosen and never the eventually-(b-1) expansion.
The unit-interval circle is [0,1) with the wrap metric, nonempty and compact; this interval model (not a complex-unit-circle model) is what cross-group users inherit.

load_bearing.statement: Let mu be sigma-finite, let T preserve mu, and let f be a finite-valued real- or complex-valued measurable representative in L^1(mu). Then A_n f converges mu-almost everywhere to a finite-valued integrable function f* satisfying f* o T = f* mu-almost everywhere and ||f*||_1 <= ||f||_1.
Assume the ultrafilter lemma. If X is a real or complex normed space, then its closed dual unit ball B_{X*} is compact in the weak-star topology sigma(X*,X). Completeness of X is not required.

Assume the ultrafilter lemma, DC, and HB. For every subset A of a real or complex Banach space X, relatively weakly compact, relatively weakly sequentially compact and relatively weakly countably compact are equivalent, with all limits and cluster points taken in the ambient weak topology.

hat-phi(xi) = integral phi(x) e^{-2 pi i x.xi} dx for Schwartz tests, and <F u, phi> = <u, F phi> for u in S'; the pairing is bilinear with no conjugation and no inverse transform on the right-hand side.

For a measure-preserving system with arbitrary measure and a real integrable representative f, if E = {x : sup_{n>=1} S_n f(x) > 0} then integral_E f dmu >= 0; neither finiteness of mu, invertibility of T nor ergodicity is assumed.
Assume the ultrafilter lemma and HB. A real or complex Banach space X is reflexive if and only if its closed unit ball B_X is compact for the weak topology sigma(X,X*).

Assume the ultrafilter lemma, DC and HB. If A is a relatively weakly countably compact subset of a real or complex Banach space X, then A is norm bounded and the weak-star closure of J_X(A) is contained in J_X(X); no cluster point or representing point is asserted to lie in A.

A complex-linear u on Schwartz space is tempered if and only if there are C >= 0 and integers N,M >= 0 with |<u,phi>| <= C max_{|alpha|<=N, |beta|<=M} sup_x |x^alpha partial^beta phi(x)| for every Schwartz test.

Assume countable choice. For a continuous self-map T of a nonempty compact metric space K, unique ergodicity (with invariant Borel probability mu) is equivalent to uniform convergence of A_n f on K to a constant for every continuous real f, and then the constant is integral_K f dmu.
Assume HB. For every real or complex normed space X the canonical image J_X(B_X) is weak-star dense in B_{X**}; no compactness or completeness hypothesis is used.

Assume HB. For a sequence in a real or complex Banach space X, its closed scalar span Y is a separable Banach space, is weakly closed in X, and its intrinsic weak topology is the relative ambient weak topology.
Assume countable choice. If alpha is irrational, the circle rotation R_alpha is uniquely ergodic and its unique invariant Borel probability is Lebesgue measure.
The circle T = [0,1) with d(x,y) = min(|x-y|, 1-|x-y|) is a nonempty compact metric space.

concerns.concern: Step 1.2 asserts 'It is regular:' for the restricted measure mu_A(E) = mu(E cap A) after proving only the inner-regularity clause. Under the cited definition ([F4], def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space plus def-radon-measure-on-an-lch-space) a regular Borel measure must additionally be Radon: finite on compacts, outer regular on every Borel set, inner regular on every open set. The missing clauses do follow (for Borel E take a compact C contained in A minus E with mu(A minus E) < mu(C) + eps and use the open complement K minus C, exploiting mu(K) < infinity; inner regularity on open sets is the same clause already proved), and regularity of mu_A and mu_{K minus A} is used in step 2.1 to place mu_1, mu_2 in the convex set P(K), so the step is load-bearing for that convex decomposition. The verification of outer regularity is not written.

Step 1.1 claims, for an arbitrary f in L^1(mu), that the convergence set and g* are strictly invariant, via the shifted-average identity A_n f(Tx) = ((n+1)/n)A_{n+1}f(x) - f(x)/n. That identity needs f finite at x (and at the iterates), whereas the sibling item thm-birkhoff-ergodic-theorem explicitly says 'finite-valued ... representative' and its step 5.1 only claims invariance after adding a null exceptional orbit set. For a representative that is infinite on a (null) set the strict-invariance claim can fail at such points, though every conclusion of this item is an a.e. statement and all the integral identities it proves are unaffected.
